tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/_Cross-cutting/Lee_2019_LoperamideMisuseWithdrawal.pdf (online-first version; pages as numbered in that PDF)
tasks.extracted: 26 registry cases coded as loperamide exposure; intent known for 18: 12 (67%) misuse, 3 (17%) attempted self-harm, 3 (17%) exploratory ingestions by children. Circumstances of misuse, more than one possible per person: taking more than labelled 8, avoiding opioid withdrawal 6, a pleasurable sensation 4. The amount was recorded in 9 cases (amounts only in the card's exposure field).

tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/_Cross-cutting/Lee_2019_LoperamideMisuseWithdrawal.pdf (online-first version; pages as numbered in that PDF)
tasks.extracted: Prolonged QTc in 10 of 26 (38.5%), 5 of whom had ventricular dysrhythmias; 9 of the 10 coded misuse (one aged 17) and 1 self-harm; 5 of the 6 with ventricular dysrhythmias had taken loperamide alone; QTc 566-749 ms in all but one; everyone with a ventricular dysrhythmia whose amount was recorded had taken far more than the label maximum; prolonged QRS in 6 (23.1%); first-degree AV block in 2; myocardial injury and infarction in 1 (3.8%); no deaths.

tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/_Cross-cutting/Lee_2019_LoperamideMisuseWithdrawal.pdf (online-first version; pages as numbered in that PDF)
tasks.extracted: Coma or CNS depression 11 (42.3%); respiratory depression 5 (printed 15.4%); bradycardia 4 (15.4%); bradypnoea 4; hypotension 3 (11.5%); tachycardia 2 (7.7%); rhabdomyolysis 3 (11.5%); acute kidney injury 3 (11.5%); aspiration pneumonitis 2 (7.7%); seizure 1. By editors' calculation 5 of 26 is 19.2%.

tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/_Cross-cutting/Lee_2019_LoperamideMisuseWithdrawal.pdf (online-first version; pages as numbered in that PDF)
tasks.extracted: 17 (65%) needed specific toxicological treatment, including an opioid antagonist in 6 (23%), sodium bicarbonate in 4 (15%), isoproterenol in 2 (8%) and amiodarone in 1; 4 (15%) were intubated, 3 of them with ventricular dysrhythmias; 2 (8%) had pacemaker intervention, both with ventricular dysrhythmias; 1 needed cardiopulmonary resuscitation, intubation, vasopressors and pacing, and survived.

tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/_Cross-cutting/Lee_2019_LoperamideMisuseWithdrawal.pdf (online-first version; pages as numbered in that PDF)
tasks.extracted: Only patients seen at the bedside by medical toxicologists, so severity is likely overestimated and exposures with few symptoms are missed; voluntary reporting; ECGs not reviewed by the authors and the QT correction method unknown; exposure not confirmed in biological samples in the vast majority of cases.

tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/_Cross-cutting/Lee_2019_LoperamideMisuseWithdrawal.pdf (online-first version; pages as numbered in that PDF)
tasks.extracted: The abstract reports seven ventricular dysrhythmias, five of them single-agent, and describes the 10 prolonged QTc cases as misuse (n = 6) and self-harm (n = 1), unlike the Results.

The printed 51.3% for 2784 of 5390 is, by editors' calculation, 51.7%.

tasks.extracted: Withdrawal significantly higher in nonholders and strongly inversely related to plasma methadone in both groups; plasma methadone before the dose 249 ng/mL in holders and 257 ng/mL in nonholders (P > .05); peak-to-trough ratio 1.9 and 1.7 (P > .05); AUC 7.4 and 8.2 mg·h/L (P > .05).

tasks.extracted: Fastest hourly fall in plasma methadone 47.6 ± 21.3 ng/mL/h in holders against 74.5 ± 40.4 in nonholders, t = 1.77, P = .09; without the two people with other opioids in urine 42.1 ± 20.8 against 74.5 ± 40.4, t = 2.10, stated P < .05; correlation of the fastest fall with the mean number of withdrawal symptoms from peak to trough r = 0.60 in all 18 (P < .01) and r = 0.67 without the two. By editors' calculation the two-sided P for t = 2.10 on 14 degrees of freedom is .054.

tasks.extracted: In the authors' earlier survey in the same programme, 34% of 114 non-selected patients regularly had withdrawal between doses and 66% did not; plasma methadone was not measured there.

tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/Methadone-Buprenorphine/Dyer_1999_InterdoseWithdrawalPKPD.pdf
tasks.extracted: The authors caution that methadone is a mixture of two mirror-image forms whose different handling can create apparent distribution effects, so a mechanism for the holder-nonholder difference should be invoked with great caution; analysis of the active form was under way.

Both eyes affected in 67 of 69 (97.1%) with details; of 81 complaints in 56 patients, changes in visual acuity 36 (44.4%), visual disturbances 29 (35.7%), central scotoma 15 (18.5%).

tasks.extracted: The authors: case reports and series are uncontrolled and can suggest hypotheses but not robust associations; data sets are inconsistent, with missing data and varied testing and follow-up, limiting generalisability.

tasks.extracted: Treatment documented for 45 patients (39.8%): stopping poppers advised for 42 (93%), 3 of whom also received oral lutein; oral lutein alone for 2; vitrectomy for 1. Compliance documented for 27, of whom 19 (70.3%) were compliant at follow-up.

tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/Alkyl-nitrites-and-inhalants/Bartolo_2023_PoppersMaculopathySR..pdf (online-first version; pages as numbered in that PDF)
tasks.extracted: Of the 9 best eyes at 0.4 logMAR or worse, only 2 were followed up and were unchanged; the authors state that it was therefore not possible to analyse the effectiveness of treatment, or of stopping poppers, on acuity.

tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/Alkyl-nitrites-and-inhalants/Bartolo_2023_PoppersMaculopathySR..pdf (online-first version; pages as numbered in that PDF)
tasks.extracted: Patient A, reported as not stopping, had acuity 0.2 in both eyes at presentation and at 40-42 months; patient B improved from 0.2 and 0.5 to −0.1 at 46-48 months with no mention of stopping, which the authors take as a sign that he had stopped. Some earlier series found no improvement in acuity and no resolution of foveal damage within 3 months of presentation despite stopping.
